newsitem.title: USA: Scherer says on track toward FY97 goals.
newsitem.headline: Scherer says on track toward FY97 goals.

text.p: R.P. Scherer Corp said it is on track to achieve its fiscal 1997 goals, provided certain trends hold up, such as a 60 percent fiscal third-quarter gain in sales of its Zydis drug delivery technology.

"On balance, we were pleased with our third-quarter performance," said chief executive Alex Erdeljan. "Particularly encouraging is the strengthening of the pharmaceutical segment as well as the continued recovery of major nutritional markets."
Shares in Scherer were off 3/8 to 52-5/8.

The company Wednesday reported net income for its third quarter ended December 31 of $15.1 million, or $0.61 per share, up 14 percent over the same period a year ago. Quarterly sales were $149.9 million, up nine percent.
"The strengthening of the U.S. dollar had the effect of reducing third-quarter net income by $0.01 per share as compared to the third-quarter last year," the company said.
Net interest expense fell 15 percent versus the prior year third quarter due to favorable short-term interest rates and internal funding of increased capital investment, it said.

"In addition to lower net interest expense, current fiscal year comparisons benefited from a reduction of the estimated consolidated effective tax rate to 28 percent versus 30 percent in the prior year period," Scherer said.
Scherer said the third-quarter sales gain came on:
--A 12 percent increase in sales of Vitamin E and other health and nutritional softgels, principally in the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia.
--An 11 percent increase in sales of over-the-counter softgel products, reflecting a strong cough/cold season.
--And the 60 percent increase in Zydis revenue.
"Prescription pharmaceutical softgel sales increased marginally in the third quarter," Scherer said.

Scherer develops and manufactures drug delivery systems and is the world's largest producer of soft gelatin capsules. The company's Zydis technology is a tablet that delivers medication by rapidly melting in the mouth.
